added to this solution, the vapour pressure of

Let X<sub>1</sub> and P$$P_1^o$$
 are the mole fraction and vapour
pressure of n-hexane in solution and X<sub>2</sub> and $$P_2^o$$

 are the mole fraction and vapour pressure of
n-heptane in solution then


550 = $$P_1^o$$ \times ${1 \over 4}$$ + $$P_2^o$$ \times ${3 \over 4}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ 2200 = $$P_1^o$$ + 3$$P_2^o$$ ....(1)


On addition of 1 more mole of n-heptane


560 = $$P_1^o$$ \times ${1 \over 5}$$ + $$P_2^o$$ \times ${4 \over 5}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ 2800 = $$P_1^o$$ + 4$$P_2^o$$ ....(2)


From (1) and (2),


$$P_1^o$$ = 400, $$P_2^o$$ = 600

questions.question:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation,
xy'- y = x2(xcosx + sinx), x > 0. if y ($$\pi $$) = $$\pi $$ then
$$y''\left( {{\pi \over 2}} \right) + y\left( {{\pi \over 2}} \right)$$ is equal to :
questions.explanation:
$$xy' - y = {x^2}(x{\mathop{\rm cosx}\nolimits}  + sinx),\,x > 0,\,y(\pi ) = \pi $$

$$y' - {1 \over x}y = x\{ x\cos x\, + \,\sin x\} $$

$$I.F. = {e^{ - \int {{1 \over 2}dx} }} = {e^{ - \ln x}} = {1 \over x}$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$y.{1 \over x} = \int {{1 \over x}.x(x\,cos\,x + sin\,x)
dx} $$

${{y \over x}}$$ = $$\int ( x\,\cos \,x + \sin \,x)dx$$

$$ = x\,\sin \,x + C$$

${{y \over x}}$$ = $$x\,\sin \,x + C$$

$$ \Rightarrow y = {x^2} = \sin \,x + cx$$

x = $$\pi $$, y = $$\pi $$

$$\pi $$ = $$\pi $$c $$ \Rightarrow $$ C = 1

$$y = {x^2}\sin x + x \Rightarrow y\left( {{\pi  \over 2}} \right) = {{{\pi ^2}} \over 4} + {\pi  \over 2}$$

$$y' = 2x\sin x + {x^2}\cos x + 1$$

y" = $$2\sin x + 2x\cos x + 2x\cos x - {x^2}\sin x$$

y" $$\left( {{\pi  \over 2}} \right) = 2 - {{{\pi ^2}} \over 4} $$


$$\Rightarrow y\left( {{\pi  \over 2}} \right)$$ + y" $$\left( {{\pi  \over 2}} \right) = 2 + {\pi  \over 2}$$

questions.question: Let $$f\left( x \right) = \int {{{\sqrt x } \over {{{\left( {1 + x} \right)}^2}}}dx\left( {x \ge 0} \right)} $$.  Then f(3) – f(1) is eqaul to :
questions.explanation:
$$\int {{{\sqrt x } \over {{{(1 + x)}^2}}}} dx(x > 0)$$

Put x = tan<sup>2</sup>$$\theta $$ $$ \Rightarrow $$ 2xdx = 2tan$$\theta $$sec<sup>2</sup>$$\theta $$d$$\theta $$

$$I = \int {{{2{{\tan }^2}\theta .{{\sec }^2}\theta } \over 2}} d\theta  = \int {2{{\sin }^2}\theta d\theta  = \int {(1 - \cos 2\theta )d\theta } } $$

$$ = \theta  - {{\sin 2\theta } \over 2} + c$$

$$ \Rightarrow f(x) = \theta  - {1 \over 2} \times {{2\tan \theta } \over {1 + {{\tan }^2}\theta }} + c$$ $$f(x) = \theta  - {{\tan \theta } \over {1 + {{\tan }^2}\theta }} + c = {\tan ^{ - 1}}\sqrt x  - {{\sqrt x } \over {1 + x}} + c$$

Now $$f(3) - f(1) = {\tan ^{ - 1}}\left( {\sqrt 3 } \right) - {{\sqrt 3 } \over {1 + 3}} - {\tan ^{ - 1}}(1) + {1 \over 2}$$

$$ = {\pi  \over 3} - {{\sqrt 3 } \over 4} - {\pi  \over 4} + {1 \over 2}$$

$$ = {\pi  \over 12} + {1 \over 2} - {{\sqrt 3 } \over 4}$$

questions.question:
Let ${{{x^2}} \over {{a^2}}} + {{{y^2}} \over {{b^2}}} = 1$$ (a > b) be a given ellipse, length of whose latus rectum is 10. If its eccentricity is the maximum value of the function,
$$\phi \left( t \right) = {5 \over {12}} + t - {t^2}$$, then a2 + b2 is equal to :
questions.explanation:
Given ellipse ${{{x^2}} \over {{a^2}}} + {{{y^2}} \over {{b^2}}} = 1$$ (a > b)

Length of latus rectum $$ = {{2{b^2}} \over a} = 10$$

$$\phi (t) = {5 \over {12}} + t - {t^2}$$

$$ = {8 \over {12}} - {\left( {t - {1 \over 2}} \right)^2}$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$\phi {(t)_{\max }} = {8 \over {12}} = {2 \over 3}$$

$$ \therefore $$ eccentricity (e) = ${2 \over 3}$$

Also, ${e^2} = 1 - {{{b^2}} \over {{a^2}}}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {4 \over 9} = 1 - {{{b^2}} \over {{a^2}}}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {{{b^2}} \over {{a^2}}} = {5 \over 9}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {{{b^2}} \over a} \times {1 \over a} = {5 \over 9}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {5 \over a} = {5 \over 9}$$

$$ \Rightarrow a = 9$$

$$ \therefore $$ ${b^2} = 5 \times 9 = 45$$

$$ \therefore $$ ${a^2} + {b^2} = 81 + 45 = 126$$

questions.question:
Let $$f(x) = \left| {x - 2} \right|$$ and g(x) = f(f(x)), $$x \in \left[ {0,4} \right]$$. Then
$$\int\limits_0^3 {\left( {g(x) - f(x)} \right)} dx$$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
$$f(x) = |x - 2|$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$f(f(x)) = \left| {|x - 2| - 2} \right| = g(x)$$

$$ \Rightarrow g(x) = \left| {|x - 2| - 2} \right| = \left\{ {\matrix{
   {|x - 4|} & {if\,x \ge 2}  \cr 
   {| - x|} & {if\,x < 2}  \cr 

 } } \right.$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$\int\limits_0^3 {(g(x) - f(x))dx} $$

$$ = \int\limits_0^3 {g(x)dx}  - \int\limits_0^3 {f(x)dx} $$

$$ = \int\limits_0^2 {| - x|dx}  + \int\limits_2^3 { - (x - 4)dx}  - \int\limits_0^2 { - (x - 2)dx}  - \int\limits_2^3 {(x - 2)dx} $$

$$ = \int\limits_0^2 {x\,dx}  - \int\limits_2^3 {(x - 4)dx}  + \int\limits_0^2 {(x - 2)dx}  - \int\limits_2^3 {(x - 2)dx} $$

$$ = \left[ {{{{x^2}} \over 2}} \right]_0^2 - \left[ {{{{x^2}} \over 2} - 4x} \right]_2^3 + \left[ {{{{x^2}} \over 2} - 2x} \right]_0^2 - \left[ {{{{x^2}} \over 2} - 2x} \right]_2^3$$

$$ = 2 - \left\{ {{9 \over 2} - 12 - 2 + 8} \right\} + \{ 2 - 4\}  - \left\{ {{9 \over 2} - 6 - 2 + 4} \right\}$$

$$ = 2 - \left\{ {{9 \over 2} - 6} \right\} - 2 - \left\{ {{9 \over 2} - 4} \right\}$$

$$ = 10 - {9 \over 2} - {9 \over 2} = {{20 - 9 - 9} \over 2} = {2 \over 2} = 1$$

questions.question: Let f be a twice differentiable function on (1, 6). If f(2) = 8, f’(2) = 5, f’(x) $$ \ge $$ 1 and f''(x) $$ \ge $$ 4, for all x $$ \in $$ (1, 6), then :
questions.explanation:
Given, $$f'(x) \ge 1$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$\int_2^5 {f'(x)} dx\, \ge \,\int_2^5 {dx} $$

$$ \Rightarrow f(5) - f(2) \ge 3$$

$$ \Rightarrow f(5) - 8 \ge 3$$

$$ \Rightarrow f(5) \ge 11$$ ...(1)

Also, $$f''(x) \ge 4$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$\int_2^5 {f''(x)} dx\, \ge \,\int_2^5 {4dx} $$

$$ \Rightarrow f'(5) - f'(2) \ge 4(3)$$

$$ \Rightarrow f'(5) - 5 \ge 12$$

$$ \Rightarrow f'(5) \ge 17$$ ...(2)

From (1) and (2),

$$f'(5) + f'(5) \ge 11 + 17$$

$$ \Rightarrow f'(5) + f'(5) \ge 28$$

questions.question:
Let $$\alpha $$ and $$\beta $$ be the roots of x<sup>2</sup> - 3x + p=0 and $$\gamma $$ and $$\delta $$ be the roots of x<sup>2</sup> - 6x + q = 0. If $$\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta $$
form a geometric progression.Then ratio (2q + p) : (2q - p) is:
questions.explanation:
$$\alpha $$ and $$\beta $$ are the roots of x<sup>2</sup> $$-$$ 3x + p = 0

$$ \therefore $$ $$\alpha $$ + $$\beta $$ = 3 and $$\alpha \beta $$ = p

$$\gamma $$ and $$\delta $$ are the roots of x<sup>2</sup> $$-$$ 6x + q = 0

$$ \therefore $$ $$\gamma $$ + $$\delta $$ = 6 and $$\gamma \delta $$ = q

Given that, $$\alpha $$, $$\beta $$, $$\gamma $$, $$\delta $$ are in G.P.

$$ \therefore $$ Let $$\alpha $$ = a, $$\beta $$ = ar, $$\gamma $$ = ar<sup>2</sup> and $$\delta $$ = ar<sup>3</sup>

As $$\alpha $$ + $$\beta $$ = 3

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a + ar = 3

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a(1 + r) = 3 ...(1)

Also $$\gamma $$ + $$\delta $$ = 6

$$ \Rightarrow $$ ar<sup>2</sup> + ar<sup>3</sup> = 6

$$ \Rightarrow $$ ar<sup>2</sup> (1 + r) = 6 ... (2)

Dividing (2) by (1),

r<sup>2</sup> = 2

$$ \Rightarrow r = \sqrt 2 $$

$$ \therefore $$ $$a = {3 \over {1 + \sqrt 2 }}$$

So, $$\alpha  = {3 \over {1 + \sqrt 2 }}$$, $$\beta  = {{3\sqrt 2 } \over {1 + \sqrt 2 }}$$, $$\gamma  = {{3 \times 2} \over {1 + \sqrt 2 }}$$, $$\delta  = {{3(2\sqrt {2)} } \over {1 + \sqrt 2 }}$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$p = \alpha \beta  = {{9\sqrt 2 } \over {{{\left( {1 + \sqrt 2 } \right)}^2}}}$$

and $$q = \gamma \delta  = {{36\sqrt 2 } \over {{{\left( {1 + \sqrt 2 } \right)}^2}}}$$

Now, ${{2q + p} \over {2q - p}}$$

$$ = {{{{72\sqrt 2 } \over {{{\left( {1 + \sqrt 2 } \right)}^2}}} + {{9\sqrt 2 } \over {{{\left( {1 + \sqrt 2 } \right)}^2}}}} \over {{{72\sqrt 2 } \over {{{\left( {1 + \sqrt 2 } \right)}^2}}} - {{9\sqrt 2 } \over {{{\left( {1 + \sqrt 2 } \right)}^2}}}}}$$

$$ = {{72\sqrt 2  + 9\sqrt 2 } \over {72\sqrt 2  - 9\sqrt 2 }}$$

$$ = {{81} \over {63}}$$

$$ = {9 \over 7}$$

questions.question:
Let $$u = {{2z + i} \over {z - ki}}$$, z = x + iy and k > 0. If the curve represented
by Re(u) + Im(u) = 1 intersects the y-axis at the points P and Q where PQ = 5, then the value of k is :
questions.explanation:
Given, z = x + iy

and $$u = {{2z + i} \over {z - ki}}$$

$$ = {{2(x + iy) + i} \over {(x + iy) - ki}}$$

$$ = {{2x + i(2y + 1)} \over {x + i(y - k)}} \times {{x - i(y - k)} \over {x - i(y - k)}}$$

$$ = {{2{x^2} + (2y + 1)(y - k) + i(2xy + x - 2xy + 2kx)} \over {{x^2} + {{(y - k)}^2}}}$$

Given, 

${\mathop{\rm Re}\nolimits} (u) + {\mathop{\rm Im}\nolimits} (u) = 1$$

$$ \Rightarrow {{2{x^2} + (2y + 1)(y - k)} \over {{x^2} + {{(y - k)}^2}}} + {{x + 2kx} \over {{x^2} + {{(y - k)}^2}}} = 1$$

$$ \Rightarrow 2{x^2} + (2y + 1)(y - k) + x + 2kx = {x^2} + {(y - k)^2}$$

This curve intersect the y-axis at point P and Q, so at point P and Q x = 0

Putting x = 0 at the above equation,

$$ \therefore $$ $$(2y + 1)(y - k) = {(y - k)^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow 2{y^2} + y - 2yk - k = {y^2} + {k^2} - 2ky$$

$$ \Rightarrow {y^2} + y - (k + {k^2}) = 0$$

Let roots of this quadratic equation y<sub>1</sub> and y<sub>2</sub>

$$ \therefore $$ Point P (0, y<sub>1</sub>) and Q (0, y<sub>2</sub>)

and ${y_{_1}} + {y_2} = 1$$ , ${y_1}{y_2} =  - k - {k^2}$$

$$ \therefore $$ ${({y_1} - {y_2})^2} = {({y_1} + {y_2})^2} - 4{y_1}{y_2}$$

$$ = 1 + 4k + 4{k^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow |{y_1} - {y_2}| = \sqrt {1 + 4k + 4{k^2}} $$

Given, PQ = 5

$$ \Rightarrow |{y_1} - {y_2}| = 5$$

$$ \Rightarrow \sqrt {1 + 4k + 4{k^2}}  = 5$$

$$ \Rightarrow {k^2} + k - 6 = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow k =  - 3,\,2$$

So, k = 2 (Given k > 0)

are 5, 7, 10, 12, 14, 15, then the absolute difference of the remaining two observations is :
questions.explanation:
Let the two remaining observations be x and y.

$$ \because $$ $$\bar x = 10 = {{5 + 7 + 10 + 12 + 14 + 15 + x + y} \over 8}$$

$$ \Rightarrow x + y = 17$$ ....(1)

$$ \because $$ ${\mathop {\rm var}} (x) = 13.5 = {{25 + 49 + 100 + 144 + 196 + 225 + {x^2} + {y^2}} \over 8} - {(10)^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {x^2} + {y^2} = 169$$ ....(2)

From (1) and (2)

(x, y) = (12, 5) or (5, 12)

So $$\left| {x - y} \right| = 7$$

questions.question:
If $$\left( {a + \sqrt 2 b\cos x} \right)\left( {a - \sqrt 2 b\cos y} \right) = {a^2} - {b^2}$$

where a > b > 0, then ${{dx} \over {dy}}\,\,at\left( {{\pi \over 4},{\pi \over 4}} \right)$$ is :
questions.explanation:
$$(a + \sqrt 2 b\cos x)(a - \sqrt 2 b\cos y) = {a^2} - {b^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow {a^2} - \sqrt 2 ab\cos y + \sqrt 2 ab\cos x - 2{b^2}\cos x\cos y = {a^2} - {b^2}$$

Differentiating both sides :

$$0 - \sqrt 2 ab\left( { - \sin y{{dy} \over {dx}}} \right) + \sqrt 2 ab( - \sin x)$$

$$ - 2{b^2}\left[ {\cos x\left( { - \sin y{{dy} \over {dx}}} \right) + \cos y( - \sin x)} \right] = 0$$

At $$\left( {{\pi  \over 4},{\pi  \over 4}} \right)$$ :

$$ab{{dy} \over {dx}} - ab - 2{b^2}\left( { - {1 \over 2}{{dy} \over {dx}} - {1 \over 2}} \right) = 0$$

$$ \Rightarrow {{dx} \over {dy}} = {{ab + {b^2}} \over {ab - {b^2}}} = {{a + b} \over {a - b}}$$; a, b > 0

questions.question:
Suppose a differentiable function f(x) satisfies the identity
f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y) + xy2 + x2y, for all real x and y.
$$\mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to 0} {{f\left( x \right)} \over x} = 1$$, then f'(3) is equal to ______.
questions.explanation:
Given, f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) + xy<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>y ...(1)

differentiating partially with respect to x,

f'(x+y) = f'(x) + 0 + y<sup>2</sup> + y(2x) [y = constant]

Put x = 0 and y = x

$$ \therefore $$ f'(x) = f'(0) + x<sup>2</sup> ....(2)

putting x = y = 0 at equation (1),

f(0) = 2f(0)

$$ \Rightarrow $$ f(0) = 0

Given, $$\mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to 0} {{f(x)} \over x} = 1$$

This is in $$ \frac{0}{0}  $$ form, so we can apply L' hospital rule.

$$\mathop {\lim }\limits_{x \to 0} {{f'(x)} \over 1} = 1$$

$$ \Rightarrow f'(0) = 1$$

Putting value of f'(0) at equation (2), we get

f'(x) = 1 + x<sup>2</sup>

$$ \therefore $$ f'(3) = 1 + 3<sup>2</sup> = 10

the polariser per revolution, is close to :
questions.explanation:
Intensity, I = 3.3 Wm<sup>–3</sup>


Area, A = 3 × 10<sup>–4</sup>
 m<sup>2</sup>


Angular speed, $$\omega $$ = 31.4 rad/s


$$I = {I_0}{\cos ^2}(\omega t)$$

$$ \Rightarrow {I_{av}} = {{{I_0}} \over 2}$$


$$ \because $$ $$\left\langle {{{\cos }^2}\theta } \right\rangle $$ = ${1 \over 2}$$, in one time period



$$ \therefore $$ $$E = {{{I_0}} \over 2} \times A \times (\Delta t)$$

and $$\Delta t = {{2\pi } \over \omega } = {{2 \times 3.14} \over {31.4}} = {1 \over 5}s$$

$$ \therefore $$ $$E = {{3.3} \over 2} \times 3 \times {10^{ - 4}} \times {1 \over 5} = 1 \times {10^{ - 4}}\,J$$

Applying momentum conservation


${m \over 2} \times {V_0} + {m \over 3} \times 0 = {m \over 2}{V_A} + {m \over 3}{V_B}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ ${{{V_0}} \over 2} = {{{V_A}} \over 2} + {{{V_B}} \over 3}$$ .....(1)


Since, collision is elastic (e = 1)


e = 1 = ${{{V_B} - {V_A}} \over {{V_0}}}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ V<sub>0</sub> = V<sub>B</sub> – V<sub>A</sub> .....(2)


On solving (1) & (2) :


V<sub>A</sub> = ${{{V_0}} \over 5}$$


Now, De-Broglie wavelength of A before collision :


$$\lambda $$<sub>0</sub> = ${h \over {{m_A}{V_0}}}$$


= ${h \over {\left( {{m \over 2}} \right){V_0}}}$$


= ${{2h} \over {m{V_0}}}$$


Final De-Broglie wavelength :


$$\lambda $$<sub>f</sub> = ${h \over {{m_A}{V_A}}}$$


= ${h \over {\left( {{m \over 2}} \right)\left( {{{{V_0}} \over 5}} \right)}}$$ = ${{10h} \over {m{V_0}}}$$


Now, $$\Delta $$\lambda $$ = $$\lambda $$<sub>f</sub> - $$\lambda $$<sub>0</sub>


= ${{10h} \over {m{V_0}}}$$ - ${{2h} \over {m{V_0}}}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\Delta $$\lambda $$ = ${{8h} \over {m{V_0}}}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\Delta $$\lambda $$ = $$4 \times {{2h} \over {m{V_0}}}$$


$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\Delta $$\lambda $$ = 4$$\lambda $$<sub>0</sub>
